documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 y/o man, yearly exam. No new concerns. No ED visits since last July.

Use: cigarettes 1 ppd (since 2016, ~8 yrs). Alcohol daily, heavy binges most nights; AUDIT-C 11. Cocaine "less than before" by his account, still at parties. Aspirin 325 most days for headaches. No GI bleeding, no abdominal pain.
PHQ-9 2.
Between construction jobs right now; expects to be back on a crew this summer.

Exam: Well developed, no distress. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck without adenopathy or thyromegaly. Heart regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, nondistended, no organomegaly. Skin: tattoos, knuckle scars, no rashes. Neuro nonfocal. No tremor.

A/P
- Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipid panel. Tdap current (2019). Declines flu discussion until fall.
- Severe alcohol use disorder, cocaine use disorder, nicotine dependence: counseled; not ready to change; declines referral.
- Antisocial personality disorder: on list.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, your labs are all normal this year, including liver tests, blood counts and cholesterol. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Phone Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Was a passenger in a friend's car yesterday evening that slid on a wet road into a guardrail; airbag went off. Says he is completely fine: no head strike, no neck or back pain, no chest or belly pain, walking normally. Did not go to the ER and doesn't want to. Partner wants him looked at. Reviewed red flags (worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, chest/abdominal pain) -> ED. Earliest he can come is 10/1 because of work; booked.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27M, seen two weeks after a minor car accident (9/17). He was the passenger; his friend was driving in the rain, lost traction and they slid into a barrier. He remembers the screech of the tires and the airbag going off. Walked away without a scratch and still has no pain anywhere. Did not seek care that night.

He allows that it was "pretty scary" in the moment but keeps coming back to the fact that nobody got hurt. Since then he's had his head down: he is on a construction job with a project deadline coming up and has been putting in overtime, and in whatever time is left he's studying for the state construction licensing exam. Asked how he's processing the accident, he says he'll deal with it when there's time and right now there are more important things to focus on. No intrusive memories or flashbacks, no nightmares, isn't avoiding cars or rides, not jumpy or on guard. Sleep short because of work and studying, not because of the accident. PHQ-9 3.

Prior ED visits Nov 2022 (police, legal) and Jul 2023 (intoxication), reviewed. Still smoking 1 ppd, drinking most nights though "less on work nights." Aspirin as before.

Exam: Vitals as charted. No bruising or seat-belt marks. Neck and spine nontender with full ROM. Chest wall and abdomen nontender. Neuro nonfocal.
Mental status: calm and cooperative, good eye contact, affect appropriate to content, speech normal. Thought process linear. No psychotic features, no signs of mania, mood described as "fine" and not depressed.

A/P
1. MVA as passenger, no injury. Normal exam. No imaging needed.
2. Stress around work deadlines and the licensing exam. He's coping by setting the accident aside, which seems to be working for now; no symptoms of acute stress disorder or PTSD. Occupational stress noted. Talked about sleep, and that alcohol will not help either the stress or the exam. Will reach out if anything about the accident starts to bother him.
3. Substance use: unchanged, brief counseling.
Flu shot at a nurse visit this month.

documents.title: Nurse Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for influenza vaccine. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Given IM L deltoid, lot recorded. VIS provided. Observed 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27M, yearly physical.

The work stress from last fall has settled; he says that stretch is behind him and he's sleeping normally. Nothing further about the accident. No new symptoms.

Use: 1 ppd, ~9 yrs now. Drinking every day, binges most nights, AUDIT-C 12. Cocaine occasionally. Aspirin most days. No hematemesis, melena or abdominal pain. PHQ-9 1.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Normal HEENT. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, liver not enlarged. No edema. Skin unremarkable apart from tattoos. No tremor.

A/P
1. Occupational stress: resolved, off the list.
2. Severe alcohol use disorder / cocaine use disorder / nicotine dependence: counseled again, no change in readiness; declines referral.
3. Antisocial personality disorder: no change.
4. CMP, CBC today. Flu shot in the fall.
RTC 1 yr.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received 2026-03-19)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 01/30/2026, 10:25 to 15:40
Patient: Jacob Healey, 28 M. Allergies: NKDA.
Home meds: aspirin 325 mg daily, OTC.

CC: nausea, vomiting, blood in vomit.

HPI: 28 yo M with antisocial personality disorder and severe alcohol and cocaine use disorders, seen here before for intoxication and a legal matter. Began vomiting early this morning, multiple times; the last episode had a small amount of bright red blood mixed in. Was at a party last night, drank heavily and used drugs including cocaine. Has a bad headache going back several days and has been taking his aspirin regularly through it. No abdominal pain. No black or bloody stools.

Social: smokes 1 ppd (~10 yrs). Heavy daily alcohol with frequent binges. Cocaine.

Exam: Well-appearing, no distress. Hemodynamically stable, vitals per flowsheet. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no rebound, no guarding.

Labs: CBC normal, hemoglobin normal. PT/INR normal.

Course: no further hematemesis during 5 hours of observation; tolerated oral fluids.

Impression: stress-related mucosal disease (acute mucosal injury of the stomach) with small-volume hematemesis, in the setting of binge alcohol, cocaine and aspirin use. Low risk; outpatient management.

Plan: omeprazole 40 mg by mouth daily for 8 weeks (Rx sent). Stop aspirin and avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen and naproxen. Stop alcohol and cocaine. Return for repeat or larger-volume bleeding, black stools, dizziness or fainting, or abdominal pain. Follow up with PCP within 1 week.

[Faxed 03/19/2026 at PCP office request]

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hey doc i was in the ER friday for throwing up, there was some blood in it. they said my stomach lining is irritated and gave me omeprazole. they said to follow up with you this week. im fine now

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know, Jacob. The doctor wants to see you this week. We have Thursday 2/5 at 4:40, I'll hold it for you. If you vomit blood again, have black stools, or feel faint, go straight back to the ER. Keep taking the omeprazole and please don't take aspirin or ibuprofen for now.

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: thursday works

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28M seen after ED visit 1/30. No ED paperwork with him and nothing sent to us; history is his.

Went to a party Thursday night, drank a lot and used cocaine. Woke up Friday morning vomiting, several times, and the last one had some bright red blood in it, "not a lot." He'd had a headache for a few days before and was taking his aspirin through it. ED did blood work which he was told was normal, watched him for a few hours, told him the stomach lining was irritated (he recalls "stress-related" something), started omeprazole 40 daily for 8 weeks and told him no aspirin. Since then: no further vomiting, no blood, no black stools, no abdominal pain, no lightheadedness. Taking the omeprazole every morning. Headache gone. Has not had aspirin since.

Drinking slowed a little this week, back to most nights; AUDIT-C 12. Smoking 1 ppd.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Conjunctivae pink. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds.

A/P
1. Hematemesis, small volume, ED dx stress-related mucosal disease with alcohol, cocaine and aspirin. Stable. Finish omeprazole 40 mg daily x 8 wks (ED Rx, on med list). Repeat CBC today. Requesting the ED record.
2. Aspirin: stopped, off his list for good.
3. Severe alcohol use disorder: this one got more traction than usual. Offered naltrexone, explained what it does and what it would mean with his drinking; also offered an addiction medicine referral. He thought about it and said no to both for now. Return precautions for bleeding reviewed.
4. Cocaine use disorder, nicotine dependence: counseled.
RTC after the omeprazole course, or sooner.

documents.title: Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, your blood count from yesterday is normal, no sign of blood loss. Keep going with the omeprazole and stay off the aspirin.

documents.title: Records Request Follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record for 1/30 still not received. Called HIM; request is in the queue. Re-sent.

documents.title: Outside Record Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record from 1/30 received and reviewed. Matches his account: small-volume hematemesis after binge drinking, cocaine and several days of aspirin; well and hemodynamically stable; CBC and PT/INR normal; ED impression stress-related mucosal disease; omeprazole 40 mg daily x 8 weeks, stop aspirin. Nothing further to act on. Our CBC 2/5 normal.

documents.title: omeprazole
documents.author: patient
documents.body: finished the omeprazole last week. no more blood or anything. do i need more

documents.title: RE: omeprazole
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. No need to continue it if you're feeling fine. Keep avoiding aspirin and ibuprofen. If you get burning, vomiting or any blood, call us. Please book a check-in in the next few months.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28M (29 later this month), follow-up; cancelled in June.

GI: nothing since February. Finished the 8 weeks of omeprazole in late March. No heartburn, no vomiting, no blood, no dark stools. Has stayed off aspirin.

Use: cigarettes 1 ppd (~10 yrs). Drinking daily, binges most nights, AUDIT-C 11, "same as always." Cocaine "now and then." PHQ-9 2.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Comfortable. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. No tremor.

A/P
1. Stress-related mucosal disease (ED 1/2026): resolved. No PPI needed. Stay off NSAIDs/aspirin.
2. Severe alcohol use disorder: revisited naltrexone and referral; still a no. Will keep offering.
3. Cocaine use disorder: on list.
4. Nicotine dependence: advised to quit; not ready.
5. Antisocial personality disorder: no change.
6. CMP, CBC today.
Follow-up booked 11/12; flu shot then if not before.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jacob, Friday's labs are normal: blood count, kidney and liver tests all fine. See you in November.
